subject: english-studies
title: Present, past and future tense
summary: Show when something happens by changing the verb.

lesson.text: The tense of a verb tells us when something happens: now, before, or later.
Simple present: things that happen now or always

items: I walk to school every day.
She walks to school every day. (add -s after he, she, it)
The sun rises in the east.

lesson.text: Simple past: things that already happened
Most verbs add -ed: walk → walked, play → played, carry → carried. Many common verbs are irregular and must be learnt.
Simple future: things that will happen
Use will + the base verb: I will travel to Owerri tomorrow.

lesson.title: Choose the tense: Yesterday, Hauwa ___ (buy) a new bag.
steps: "Yesterday" tells us it has already happened: past tense.
Yesterday, Hauwa bought a new bag.

lesson.text: Look for time words: yesterday, last week, ago (past); every day, always (present); tomorrow, next year (future).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: Last Sunday, we ___ to church.
questions.explanation: "Last Sunday" is in the past, and go is irregular: go → went.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: My father ___ the newspaper every morning.
questions.explanation: "Every morning" is a habit, so use the simple present. After "my father" (he), add -s: reads.

questions.prompt: What is the past tense of "bring"?
questions.explanation: Bring is irregular: bring → brought. "Bringed" is a common mistake.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the future tense?
questions.explanation: Will + base verb (will cook) shows the future.

questions.prompt: Find the mistake: "Two days ago, Tunde eat all the bread."
questions.explanation: "Two days ago" is in the past, so eat must change to ate.
